To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we can find all motifs common to two or more sequences in time and space linear to the size of the sequences, and (2) we can succinctly encode these motifs in space linear to the number of motifs.

(1) we have developed a linear time algorithm that enumerates all common motifs of length k, (2) we have developed an algorithm that encodes the output of the enumeration in succinct data structures that require time and space proportional to the number of motifs and not to the number of sequences, (3) we have developed algorithms that parallelize the enumeration, and (4) we have developed efficient algorithms for enumerating all motifs of a given length that are common to a set sequences.

we have given a linear-time and space algorithm for enumerating motifs common to multiple sequences, and that the time and memory requirements of the algorithm depend on the number motifs, not directly the length of the motifs.
